title: The Walt Disney Company Q1 Fiscal 2025 Earnings Report
summary: This document outlines The Walt Disney Company's Q1 fiscal 2025 financial results and key segment highlights. It reports revenue growth to $24.7 billion, alongside significant increases in pre-tax income, diluted EPS, total segment operating income, and adjusted EPS. Segment results detail operating income gains in Entertainment (spurred by Direct-to-Consumer growth and Moana 2) and Sports (driven by ESPN ad revenue), while Experiences operating income remained flat due to weather impacts from Hurricanes Milton and Helene and launch costs for the Disney Treasure cruise ship. The report also includes explanatory footnotes on non-GAAP financial measures and Disney+ Hotstar India advertising figures.

title: Disney Fiscal 2025 Guidance, Segment Outlook, and CEO Commentary
summary: This text provides The Walt Disney Company's guidance, operational outlook, and executive commentary for fiscal 2025. It outlines the accounting impacts of Star India's deconsolidation, specific Q2 segment expectations—including a slight decline in Disney+ subscribers, sports-related cost pressures, and cruise line pre-opening expenses—and full-year targets including high-single digit adjusted EPS growth, $15 billion in cash from operations, and segment operating income gains. It also includes a statement from CEO Robert A. Iger celebrating strong Q1 box office returns, streaming profitability, and digital expansion, along with accounting footnotes.

title: Summarized Financial and Segment Results for Q1 Fiscal 2025 and 2024
summary: This document page presents summarized first-quarter financial and segment results comparing fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2024. It outlines overall corporate metrics—such as revenue, pre-tax income, diluted EPS, and cash flows—along with a detailed segment breakdown of revenue and operating income across Entertainment, Sports, and Experiences. It also includes footnotes detailing intersegment eliminations and defining non-GAAP financial measures.

title: DISCUSSION OF FIRST QUARTER SEGMENT RESULTS

nodes.title: Star India
nodes.summary: This text discusses the Company's first-quarter segment results, covering the formation and ownership accounting of the Star India joint venture with Reliance Industries Limited, alongside detailed revenue and operating income metrics for the Entertainment segment across Linear Networks, Direct-to-Consumer, and Content Sales/Licensing and Other.

nodes.title: Entertainment
nodes.summary: This text provides Disney's Q1 fiscal segment financial results, focusing on the Star India joint venture transaction with Reliance Industries, detailed financial performance and subscriber/ARPU metrics for the Entertainment division (encompassing Linear Networks, Direct-to-Consumer, and Content Sales/Licensing), and operational results for the Sports segment across ESPN and Star India.

nodes.title: Sports
nodes.summary: This text details financial and operating metrics for Disney's direct-to-consumer services, content sales, and sports operations for the quarter ended December 28, 2024. It highlights ARPU growth across Domestic and International Disney+, Hulu Live TV + SVOD, and ESPN+, alongside steady Hulu SVOD Only results. It also covers the theatrical-driven turnaround in Content Sales/Licensing led by 'Moana 2', overall Sports segment financials, specific operational cost and revenue drivers for Domestic ESPN, International ESPN, and Star India, and sequential subscriber and ARPU metrics for ESPN+.

nodes.title: Experiences
nodes.summary: This text provides a quarterly financial review of the Experiences segment for the quarter ended December 28, 2024, compared to the prior-year quarter, detailing revenues and operating income for domestic parks, international parks, and consumer products. It outlines the operational drivers behind domestic results—such as hurricane impacts, attendance declines, and cruise expansion costs—and international performance driven by attendance and guest spending growth. Furthermore, it reports other financial information, specifically an increase in corporate shared expenses due to a legal settlement and an impairment loss related to the Star India Transaction.

summary: This section provides a comprehensive review of Disney's first-quarter segment results for the period ended December 28, 2024. It details the financial performance, operational drivers, and subscriber/ARPU metrics across the Entertainment, Sports, and Experiences segments, while addressing corporate shared expenses and the accounting, operational impact, and impairment loss associated with the Star India joint venture transaction with Reliance Industries Limited.

title: OTHER FINANCIAL INFORMATION

nodes.title: Experiences Segment Financial Results and Other Financial Information
nodes.summary: This page summarizes the quarterly financial results for the Experiences segment, highlighting domestic performance impacted by hurricanes, inflation, and cruise fleet expansion, alongside international operating growth driven by attendance and guest spending. It also outlines other financial information, including a $152 million increase in corporate and unallocated shared expenses due to a legal settlement and a $143 million impairment loss from the Star India Transaction.

nodes.title: Financial Review: Net Interest Expense, Investee Income, and Income Taxes
key_items: Equity in the Income of Investees
nodes.summary: This text provides a quarterly financial comparison between the periods ended December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023, across three key areas: net interest expense, equity in the income of investees, and income taxes. Net interest expense rose as lower interest expense was outweighed by reduced investment income, lower cash balances, and investment losses. Equity in investee income decreased due to lower earnings from A+E and losses from the India joint venture. Additionally, the effective income tax rate rose to 27.8%, driven by a non-cash tax charge related to the Star India Transaction, mitigated partly by favorable prior-year tax adjustments and lower foreign tax rates.

nodes.title: Noncontrolling Interests, Cash from Operations, and Free Cash Flow Overview
nodes.summary: This document covers financial results for noncontrolling interests and operating cash flows. It details the decrease in net income attributable to noncontrolling interests due to the prior-year accretion of NBC Universal's Hulu interest, and outlines the $1.0 billion increase in cash provided by operations, driven by lower tax payments and higher Entertainment operating income, partially offset by higher production spending and sports rights timing. It also presents comparative free cash flow figures and notes free cash flow's non-GAAP status.

nodes.title: Capital Expenditures and Depreciation Expense Breakdown by Segment
nodes.summary: This text provides segment-level financial data for capital expenditures and depreciation expense for the quarters ended December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023. It reports that capital expenditures increased from $1.3 billion to $2.5 billion due to cruise ship fleet expansion in the Experiences segment, and details an increase in total depreciation expense from $823 million to $909 million across Entertainment, Sports, Experiences, and Corporate segments.

summary: This section provides supplementary quarterly financial information, detailing Experiences segment performance, corporate costs, and Star India Transaction impacts alongside net interest expense, investee income, and income tax rates. It also reviews net income from noncontrolling interests, operating and free cash flows, and segment breakdowns of capital expenditures and depreciation expenses.

title: THE WALT DISNEY COMPANY CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF INCOME (unaudited; $ in millions, except per share data)
summary: This text presents The Walt Disney Company's unaudited condensed consolidated statements of income for the quarters ended December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023, outlining total revenues, operating and non-operating expenses, income taxes, net income (total and attributable to Disney and noncontrolling interests), basic and diluted earnings per share, and share count figures.

title: THE WALT DISNEY COMPANY CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEETS (unaudited; $ in millions, except per share data)
summary: The text presents The Walt Disney Company's unaudited Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets as of December 28, 2024, and September 28, 2024, and the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the quarters ended December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023. It outlines the company's financial position across assets, liabilities, and shareholders' equity, as well as operational, investing, and financing cash flows leading to ending cash balances.

title: DTC PRODUCT DESCRIPTIONS AND KEY DEFINITIONS
summary: The text details the DTC product offerings, distribution channels, and subscriber metrics for Disney+, ESPN+, and Hulu. It provides definitions for paid subscribers and bundles, defines International Disney+, and outlines the revenue inclusion, allocation rules, and subscriber-averaging formulas used to calculate Average Monthly Revenue Per Paid Subscriber.

title: NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES
summary: This text provides definitions, investor rationales, and quantitative reconciliations for the Company's key non-GAAP financial measures—diluted EPS excluding certain items, total segment operating income, and free cash flow—for the quarters ended December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023. It notes the limitations of these non-GAAP metrics, explains why forward-looking GAAP EPS reconciliations cannot be provided, and details adjustments related to restructuring, joint ventures, capital expenditures, and TFCF/Hulu acquisition-related amortization.

title: FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS
key_items: PREPARED EARNINGS REMARKS AND CONFERENCE CALL INFORMATION; CONTACTS:
PREPARED EARNINGS REMARKS AND CONFERENCE CALL INFORMATION
summary: This text provides The Walt Disney Company's forward-looking statements disclaimer, outlining internal execution risks and external economic, competitive, and regulatory factors that could cause actual results to differ from expectations, while pointing to SEC filings for further risk factors. Additionally, it defines corporate entity terms, provides details for accessing the February 5, 2025 earnings call webcast and prepared remarks, and lists contact information for corporate communications and investor relations.
